messages:
maria_g: quick question — onboarding 'Saffron-12B' finished evals but the upstream license says `research-only` + 'no derivatives' and has an attribution clause. we're planning int8 quantization and to serve it from Hosted API. does that count as redistribution or creating a derivative? cc @elena_legal

alex_h: short context — our quant pipeline produces a weight file (`saffron-12b.int8.pt`) that we'd normally store on disk and load into the runtime. intent is to serve for customers on hosted & offer Dedicated pools.

maria_g: also considering not persisting quantized weights (quantize on startup into memory) to avoid writing a modified artifact to disk. curious if that changes the legal view.

elena_legal: quick take: hosting a model for users to query (SaaS) is often treated differently than distributing copies, but the 'no derivatives' term can be triggered by transforming the weights (eg quantization). it's license-specific. need to see the exact clause text. can you paste the license snippet?

maria_g: here it is (excerpt):
```
Use permitted for research purposes only. No modification or derivative works allowed. Redistribution of model weights or derivative weights is prohibited. Attribution to upstream required in any public work.
```

alex_h: ok. two practical questions: 1) Is hosting a quantized version the same as redistributing? 2) If we provide Dedicated customers access to a node that holds the quantized weights, are we effectively distributing?

elena_legal: answers: 1) Likely borderline. If we keep modified weights only on our servers and never transfer them to third parties, arguable it's a hosted service. But the 'no modification/derivative' clause could still apply because quantization is a transformation. 2) If we copy quantized weights into a customer's environment (e.g., package into a container or push files to their infra), that is redistribution — high risk.

devon_p: for Dedicated, customers usually expect us to manage the image; we often build a container containing model artifacts and deploy into their VPC. that would involve transferring artifacts — looks like redistribution per elena.

maria_g: for Private (customer-managed on-prem), customers bring their own weights normally. we could require them to provide upstream weights and run our quantization job locally — that avoids us redistributing modified weights.

alex_h: note: evals show int8 gives ~2.3x throughput improvement and minor quality delta on our chat eval set. quantization's value for Hosted/Dedicated is material for latency/cost.

maria_g: question: is in-memory ephemeral quantization (do quantize at runtime, never write to disk, never hand off files) a safer option?

elena_legal: ephemeral in-memory transformations reduce redistribution risk but don't eliminate derivative concerns. licensors sometimes define 'derivative' broadly. best path: 1) ask upstream for a written clarification/exception for hosting & quantization, 2) provide technical details (we do in-memory only for Hosted; Dedicated requires customer consent or we provide only original weights), 3) if they refuse, fallback: host unquantized model or choose a permitted model. I can draft the clarification email.

maria_g: thanks. i'll draft and attach our eval summary + quant pipeline snippet. drafting now.

alex_h: adding the quant command we used for the reference bench:
```
python tools/quantize.py --model saffron-12b --mode int8 --output /tmp/saffron.int8.pt --no-save-optimizer
```

maria_g: tagging request: need legal review + IP intake before we push to Dedicated or host publicly. deadline — some customers asked for Hosted access next week.

elena_legal: i'll open an IP review and will also send the clarification email to the model owner. please attach the exact license text, quant workflow docs, and the eval numbers.

ip-review-bot: IP review created: IR-2026-1145. Assigned to elena_legal. Please attach docs to the ticket.

devon_p: if upstream denies hosting, fallback plan: (a) offer unquantized Hosted with restricted SLAs, (b) recommend customers use Private + run quant locally, or (c) swap to an alternative permissive model.

maria_g: ok i'll route the ask and update this thread with responses. thanks all. :thumbsup:

elena_legal: will review the draft before sending. keep me looped.
